title: Animal and Trickster Tales
summary: How the American Folklife Center connects animal storytelling, trickster characters, archival recordings, and competing interpretations of Br’er Rabbit.

title: Folktales and Oral Storytelling: Collection Guide
summary: An entry point into oral histories, folktale genres, community storytelling traditions, and the Library’s collections and finding aids.

title: Anansi the Spider — World Treasures
summary: An exhibition section placing Anansi within Ghanaian, Caribbean, and African diaspora storytelling and the illustrated-book tradition.

title: Ananse: Folktale and Fairy Tale Resources
summary: A teaching and discovery guide to Ananse or Anansi, including spelling variants and references to retellings of the Akan spider stories.

title: Telling Tradition of Nasreddin Anecdotes
summary: An official heritage listing describing how humorous Nasreddin anecdotes circulate across several communities and remain part of living traditions.

title: Raven Story — Native American Lifeways
summary: A museum presentation of a Raven narrative that offers a specific interpretive context for Indigenous storytelling rather than a universal account.

title: First Peoples in Māori Tradition
source_name: Te Ara — Encyclopedia of New Zealand
summary: New Zealand encyclopedia material introducing traditions involving early ancestral and culture-hero narratives, including Māui.

title: The Myth of Anansi, the Trickster Spider
summary: An educator-led illustrated lesson that follows Anansi’s attempt to obtain stories from the sky god, with supporting background and creator credits.

title: The Myth of Loki and the Master Builder
summary: A Norse-storytelling lesson focused on the bargain to build Asgard’s wall, with prompts for further reading about surviving sources.

title: The Trickster in the Arts
source_name: The San Francisco Jung Institute Library Journal / JSTOR
summary: A 1981 article by John Beebe addressing the trickster in the arts. Bibliographic details are verified, but the full text was not independently accessible; JSTOR access may be restricted.

title: “Trickster” and Tragicomedian
summary: Julie Hamilton examines Woody Allen's films through comedy, tragedy, moral ambiguity and questions of existence, considering the modern tragicomedian as a cultural provocateur.

title: Alan Watts – The Joker
summary: A 2012 post presenting an audio excerpt and unofficial transcription of Alan Watts on the Joker and Fool as outsiders who expose the social games that people take seriously.

title: A Note on the “Sly Man”
summary: A discussion of Gurdjieff's 'sly man' method: noticing habitual reactions, deliberately acting otherwise, and directing the resulting inner friction toward conscious aims.

title: The Jester’s Banquet
summary: Max Dunbar reviews Russell Brand's Revolution through the tension between political satire, celebrity and serious dissent, asking whether the public provocateur is reformer or performer.

title: Archetypes: Jester
summary: Writer Ariel Hudnall profiles the Jester as an archetype in fiction, covering motivations, comic relief, shadow traits, humor as a defense, and illustrative characters.

title: Crazy Wisdom — Fool, Clown, Jester and Trickster
summary: A comparative essay on the fool, clown, jester and trickster, exploring their different roles in exposing hypocrisy, challenging convention and offering forms of 'crazy wisdom.'

title: Joker — Shadow and Persona Issues
summary: Psychotherapist Toby Ingham uses the film Joker to explain Jungian shadow and persona, exploring the tension between the face presented to the world and concealed aspects of personality.

title: The Joker and Jung’s Shadow
source_name: The Blackwell Philosophy and Pop Culture Series
summary: Ashley L. Whitaker interprets Arthur Fleck's Joker through the Jungian shadow, considering disorder, social marginalization and the consequences of refusing to confront destructive impulses.

title: Brand Archetypes: The Jester
summary: An applied branding guide to the Jester archetype, explaining how humor and perspective-shifting shape marketing, with examples including M&M's, Geico, Old Spice and Taco Bell.

title: Gray Jedi and the Subtle Art of Gray-walking
summary: A speculative Jester Guru Chronicles essay using Gray Jedi imagery to explore sacred humor, nuance, paradox and challenges to ideological extremes rather than historical Star Wars canon.

title: The Trickster
summary: Screenwriter Aadip Desai collects trickster characters across mythology and popular culture, emphasizing boundary crossing, mischief, moral ambiguity and truth-to-power storytelling.
